cases.narrationEn: Hoya the tiger opens a glowing storybook. Whoosh! We land in Joseon, Korea, almost 600 years ago. Here lived King Sejong, the fourth king of the Joseon dynasty.
facts: King Sejong was the fourth king of the Joseon dynasty; he reigned from 1418 to 1450.
In 1443 (recorded in the 12th lunar month of Sejong's 25th year), King Sejong himself created 28 letters and called them Hunminjeongeum.

cases.narrationEn: The finished Annals were kept in special archives called {kw:sago}. During a great war in the 1590s, the copies kept in Seoul, Chungju and Seongju were lost. Only the Jeonju copy survived.
facts: The Annals were kept in archives (sago). In the Imjin War, which began in 1592, the copies at the Chunchugwan in Seoul and at Chungju and Seongju were lost; only the Jeonju copy survived.

cases.narrationEn: Scientists can study the weather notes in the {kw:seungjeongwon-ilgi}, written day after day for nearly 300 years, to learn about nature in the past.
facts: The Seungjeongwon Ilgi recorded the weather daily over 288 years (1623–1910), and these records can be used for natural-science research.

cases.narrationEn: Almost 800 years later, the blocks are still kept safe at Haeinsa. Hoya whispers, "{kw:sojunghaeyo}, they're precious." Next time, let's find out how the buildings protect them!
facts: The Tripitaka Koreana woodblocks are kept at Haeinsa Temple on Gayasan Mountain in Hapcheon, South Gyeongsang Province, in the halls Beopbojeon and Sudarajang.
The woodblocks were carved in Goryeo between 1237 and 1248 (the 24th to 35th years of King Gojong).
